_about: The registry of the review dialog's layout options. build.mjs turns every entry into one section of demo.html. The id is the id the kit knows the option by (research/_review/review.js UI_OPTIONS or rvKit.registerUiOption), so the preview can switch it with ?rvui=<id>. Add an entry here when an option joins the kit, run `node research/review-kit-v2/build.mjs`, and the demo shows it.

groups.title: The component first: the dialog's space
Reading and moving through a step
Knowing where you are, and carrying on
Judging faster, and never losing a verdict
What comes after the last step

options.title: Near-fullscreen dialog
options.what: The dialog takes 99% of the window instead of 94% by 92%, and its header, margins and gaps get tighter.
options.why: Every pixel the chrome gives back goes to the component you are judging; on a 1920 by 1080 window the component gains about 120 px of width and 80 px of height.
expected: Off: a wide grey margin around the dialog and a tall header with padding.
On: the dialog nearly touches the window edge, the header is one slim row, the frames sit closer together.
The close button, the step line and the title all stay in the header row.
options.look: Compare the margin round the dialog and the height of the header with the option off and on; nothing may be cut at 1280 or at phone width.

options.title: Each title once
options.source: Kenny, 2026-10-18 15:15: "the title seems to not even use the full horizontal space" and the section title standing three times.
options.what: The section title stands once per frame, in the frame's own head; the topic heading above it and the section's own heading inside it are not repeated.
options.why: Three copies of one title cost two lines of height and make you read the same words three times before you reach the component.
expected: Off: the section title above the frame, in the frame head and again inside the section.
On: one title, in the frame head, with the play and speed buttons beside it; the theme stays in the dialog header.
Screen readers still find the topic heading; it is only not drawn.
options.look: Count the places the section title is written, with the option off and on.

options.title: What to look at, once per step
options.source: Kenny, 2026-10-18 15:15: "There are sections to the right with the exact same text"; the same idea as the theme paragraph once per theme run.
options.what: A look-at paragraph that is the same in several sections of one step is shown once under the theme's name in the side column, and only the lines that differ stay under their section.
options.why: The theme's own paragraph was repeated under every section of the step, a screen of identical text in the column you use to judge.
expected: Off: the same paragraph under each of the step's sections.
On: that paragraph once under the theme's name; a section with its own line keeps it.
Every section still has its row with Not approved, its note and its choices.
options.look: In the side column, read how many times the same sentence appears with the option off and on.

options.title: Compact controls
options.source: Kenny, 2026-10-18 15:15: "they can be much more inline to maximise space usage".
options.what: The controls of a component flow side by side across the full width, each group's label and buttons on one line, in the package's small button size.
options.why: Four groups fit in two lines instead of a tall stack of left-aligned rows with huge buttons, so the component starts higher; the controls stay directly above their component.
expected: Off: one group per row, large buttons, most of the width empty.
On: groups side by side that wrap at the window's edge, small package buttons, one word "Controls" as the plate's title.
Pressing a button still changes the component and the pressed one stays pressed.
options.look: Look at the height of the controls plate and at whether any button is cut or touches the plate's edge.

options.title: Full-width text
options.source: Kenny, 2026-10-18 15:15: "the demo's intro text is a narrow left column" and the empty space beside it.
options.what: The section's intro and Expected text run the whole width of the frame instead of a narrow column, and the page margin inside the frame gets tighter.
options.why: A line that is 80 characters wide in a 1700 px frame leaves most of the frame empty and makes the paragraph tall; at full width it is two lines.
expected: Off: the intro paragraph is a narrow column with empty space to its right.
On: the paragraph uses the frame's width and takes fewer lines.
On a phone nothing changes, the column was already the whole width.
options.look: Compare the number of lines of the intro paragraph and the empty space to its right.

options.title: Slim side column
options.source: Claude's proposal, from Kenny's 2026-10-18 15:15 "narrower or merged" and "reachable without scrolling".
options.what: The side column is narrower, and Previous, Next and Approve stay pinned at its foot while its rows scroll.
options.why: The component gains the width and the buttons you press most are always under your thumb, however many sections the step has.
expected: Off: a 22 rem column; the buttons sit at the end of the rows and scroll away on a long step.
On: a column of about 17% of the window; the rows scroll, the three buttons and the key line stay at the foot.
Approve, Previous and Next keep working with the keys Up, Left and Right.
options.look: Scroll the side column on a step with several sections: the buttons must not move.

options.title: Jump list of sections
options.what: One chip per section of the step in the header: a press scrolls to that section, and the section in view is marked in the chips and in its row.
options.why: On a step with three or more tall sections you see at once where you are and can go to the one you want without scrolling past the others.
expected: Off: no chips; the rows in the side column are the only way to jump.
On: numbered chips in the header; the marked one follows the scroll and its row gets a rule at the start.
At 1600 px and narrower the chips take their own row under the header and scroll sideways.
options.look: Scroll the frames and watch the marked chip follow; press another chip.

options.title: Remaining line
options.source: Claude's proposal, from Kenny's wish for hard numbers.
options.what: One plain line in the dialog's header: the step you are on, the pairs left in this part, the pairs left in all open reviews, and the time left at your pace. The same counts stand on every Agenda row.
options.why: A long review stops feeling endless when it says where it ends; the numbers are exact and count only what this round asks.
expected: Off: the header has no counts.
On: a thin line of plain text, for example "Step 1 of 22 here · this part: 55 of 55 pairs left · all open reviews: 861 of 861 left"; the pace appears after five steps of yours.
The line is text, never a pill, and takes no row of its own in the near-fullscreen header.
options.look: Read the line in the header and check that no number is shortened.

options.title: Continue where you left off
options.what: The Agenda gets one Continue button at the top that opens the part you were in, at the step you were at, with your pressed states back.
options.why: No hunting for the part and the step after a break; the dialog also remembers the scroll and the states you pressed.
expected: Off: the Agenda lists the parts; you open one and the dialog starts at its first open step.
On: a Continue button names the part, the theme and the step and reopens exactly there.
This preview shows the Agenda with one part half judged.
options.look: Find the Continue button at the top of the Agenda and read what it names.

kp-demo-review:kpadopt56-choose:resume.title: Picker with the usual on top · Synthwave

options.title: Key legend
options.what: One always-visible line under the header with the keys: Up approves, Down or C rejects the focused section, Q and S move the focus, X ticks Not approved, the arrows step, W undoes, B shows what you rejected, Esc closes.
options.why: No hesitation about which key does what; all of them are left-hand keys on an AZERTY keyboard, the right hand stays on the arrows.
expected: Off: no line; the keys are only in the footer text of the side column.
On: one row of small keys with their words, hidden on a phone where there are no keys.
Nothing is hidden when it is off, only the reminder.
options.look: Read the line and check that every key does what its words say.

options.title: Undo the last verdict
options.what: Key W undoes the last approve or reject and returns to that step with its boxes as they were. The journal gets a line saying so; nothing is ever deleted.
options.why: A mis-press costs one key instead of finding the row again, and you stop slowing down for fear of a slip.
expected: Off: a slip is fixed by walking back and unticking.
On: W steps back to the step you just left, with its ticks as they were before you pressed Approve.
The answer you paste still says only what you finally decided.
options.look: Approve a step, press W and check the step and its boxes come back.

options.title: Rejected so far
options.what: A button and the key B open a plate over the stage, never docked: your rejections with their notes, the defaults you changed and the options you removed; a press on a line jumps to that pair.
options.why: You can see your own rejections before you move on, without a window at the end of the review.
expected: Off: no plate; rejected rows stay in their step.
On: B opens a plate over the stage listing what you rejected; Esc closes it and it covers nothing while closed.
This preview rejects the first section and opens the plate.
options.look: Open the plate and check it is opaque and readable and the lines are whole.

options.title: Approve the rest of a theme
options.source: Claude's proposal; off unless you choose it.
options.what: Key G approves the rest of a theme after three approvals in a row in it, after a line that says how many pairs it covers. The journal and the answer say "approved unseen", and it can be undone for ten seconds.
options.why: When a family of themes is plainly alike, the last steps cost one key; it is a deliberate action with a written trail, never silent.
expected: Off: every step is approved by you.
On: after three approvals G offers the rest, says the count, and records them as unseen.
It is off by default because it approves without looking.
options.look: Check the confirm line names the number of pairs and says unseen.

options.title: Reason chips
options.what: Under Not approved a few small chips (spacing, colour, motion, wrong state, off-theme, broken) add a tag to the note with one click or the keys 1 to 6.
options.why: A rejection costs two seconds instead of twenty words and reaches the builder as something it can sort; nothing is required.
expected: Off: only the note.
On: chips under the box once it is ticked; a chip adds or removes its tag in the note.
A rejection without a chip or a note stays valid.
options.look: Tick Not approved on the first row and check the chips sit under it and keep clear of the note.

options.title: After the last step: the next part
options.what: After the last open step of a part, the dialog goes on to the next part that still has open pairs, after a two-second line (Esc goes back to the Agenda), instead of returning to the Agenda.
options.why: No Agenda, click and page load between parts, and no break in the thread; it never reopens a part that is already judged.
expected: Off: the end of a part goes back to the Agenda.
On: the end of a part goes on to the next part with open pairs; your verdicts are written first.
This preview shows the setting in the Agenda's flow panel.
options.look: Find the flow panel on the Agenda and read the setting.

options.title: Tonight playlist
options.source: Claude's proposal; off unless you choose it.
options.what: A Start Tonight entry on the Agenda walks every open part as one run over the existing part pages, with no merged page and no merged ids.
options.why: One walk through all the open work, without choosing a part each time; verdicts stay filed per part.
expected: Off: the Agenda lists the parts only.
On: a Start Tonight entry appears and starts the run.
This preview shows the Agenda with the entry.
options.look: Find the Start Tonight entry on the Agenda.

options.title: Tonight order: by theme
options.what: A Tonight run goes theme by theme (all of one theme across the parts, then the next) instead of part by part.
options.why: Your eye keeps one palette for many pairs in a row, which makes comparing easier and tires less.
expected: Off: part by part.
On: each part page asks only the theme that is on turn in that visit.
This preview shows the order setting in the Agenda's flow panel.
options.look: Find the order setting in the flow panel on the Agenda.
